Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network CAPTURE, collaborate with academic, healthcare, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on wireless endoscopy.

As part of the CAPTURE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027.

Your immediate leader will be the unit leader of Colourlab.
About the project
The CAPTURE project is an EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to advancing wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) through developments in computer vision and artificial intelligence. The project aims to improve image-based diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment by developing methods that reduce clinicians’ workload, enhance imaging quality, and support more accurate and timely diagnoses.

CAPTURE combines research with a strong focus on doctoral training, preparing a new generation of researchers to work at the interface of technology and medicine. The consortium brings together expertise from academia, industry, and hospitals, ensuring that the research is both scientifically rigorous and clinically relevant.

The project focuses on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), reflecting its growing prevalence in Europe. As many of the methods developed have broader applicability, the project will also consider other gastrointestinal diseases. These goals will be achieved through the recruitment and training of 15 doctoral candidates in an international and intersectoral environment, providing interdisciplinary expertise across the technical, clinical, and applied aspects of WCE.
Duties of the position
The WCEs currently applied for gastrointestinal imaging mainly contain RGB cameras. This is not necessarily optimal for imaging inside the gastrointestinal system.  

This project aims at studying multispectral imaging of the gastrointestinal system, enabling multispectral imaging capabilities for WCE. The focus will be on finding optimal spectral bands for relevant pathologies as well as efficient design of spectral imaging process.  

The goals for this PhD project are:   

• Determine the most suitable spectral bands for detection and classification of target pathologies under given resource constraints like sensor size, power consumption etc. 
• Investigate methods for improved pathology detection and visualisation for suggested multispectral approach.  
• Experimental verification of spectral bands using emulated capsule. 
This will include application of advanced hyperspectral equipment to measure target pathologies, construction of custom endoscope for experimental verification, as well as testing at Innlandet Hospital Trust.

Key responsibilities

• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate.
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above.
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the Colourlab research group.
• Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person across the CAPTURE partner institutions and contribute to CAPTURE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to University of Thessaly in Greece and University of Granada in Spain.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have solid experience with imaging or image processing. 
• You must have very good programming skills.
• At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, imaging science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
• You must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
Preference may be given to candidates with:

• Background in multi- or hyperspectral imaging.
• Experience with hardware and electronics in general.
• Excellent analytical and communication skills.
• Ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary environment.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to:  

• Work independently and in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals, and get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity, and be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
 

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
• As an employee in Norway, the successful candidate will normally be a member of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme, which provides access to public healthcare and social security benefits in accordance with applicable legislation and regulations.
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance and Mobility Allowance. In addition, a family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations.

A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary.

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. Incomplete applications will not be prioritised.

The application must include: 

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• CV 
• Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed master’s degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) 
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Possibly publications and other relevant research work
•  Possibly certificates
• Names and contact information of at least two relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

Evaluation processApplications will be assessed by an expert committee based on the qualifications and documentation submitted by the applicants. The evaluation will consider academic achievements, the quality and relevance of the applicant's educational background, research potential, and suitability for the position. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview. The final appointment will be made in accordance with the applicable regulations for employment at the university. 
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Researcher Pål Anders Floor,  email paal.anders.floor@ntnu.no 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR at the department: hr@idi.ntnu.no.

NTNU is the foremost technical university in Norway, located in Trondheim. NTNU NanoLab is a 700 m² cleanroom facility opened in 2009, and a central part of NTNU’s strategic initiative for Nanoscience, Nanotechnology and Functional Materials. The Faculty of Natural Sciences is the host faculty.

NTNU NanoLab is an open-access cleanroom serving both academia and industry, equipped for nano-structuring and characterisation using physical, chemical and biological methods. On average 300 users from diverse scientific fields use the facility each year. NTNU NanoLab is part of the Norwegian national infrastructure for micro- and nanofabrication (NorFab), the Nordic Nanolab Network (NNN) and the European cleanroom consortium EuroNanoLab. The permanent staff includes the Director, six service and process engineers, and the Head of Laboratory.

The Head of Laboratory is a technical administrator who acts as the leader of the engineering team and is the interface between our users, the University and the NanoLab. The engineers are the competence holders for the cleanroom and its instrumentation. The leader role requires in-depth knowledge of all aspects of running an advanced cleanroom infrastructure, including but not limited to chemical handling (toxic, explosive, and pyrophoric gases; nanoparticles), air filtration, gas supply systems, building management systems (BMS), and laboratory information management systems (LIMS) as well as advanced scientific equipment. Some prior experience in maintenance and repair of scientific instrumentation is therefore required.

We are a positive, international team with good opportunities for both professional and personal development. NTNU NanoLab operates as a dynamic environment with a flat hierarchy where every employee has a genuine impact on the operation.

Your immediate leader will be the Director NTNU NanoLab
Duties of the position
Job Description

The Head of Laboratory is responsible for administrating and managing the operation of NTNU’s cleanroom facilities and supporting infrastructure. The position works closely with the leader of Technical Operations and reports to the Director of NTNU NanoLab, who holds personnel responsibility. If the perfect candidate cannot be found, NanoLab would have to withdraw the position for further assessement.

• Work management and coordination of a team comprising 6 engineers, 7 PhD duty workers and 7 student assistants

• Continual improvement of existing administrative and infrastructure routines, and development of new ones, to ensure an efficient and safe work environment

• Representation of NTNU NanoLab at national and international networking meetings
• Coordination of investments and major cleanroom rebuilds

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus on professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

Supply chains are at the core of industrial competitiveness, sustainability, and resilience. As industries face the twin transitions of digitalization and the Green Shift, advances in artificial intelligence, data analytics, and automation are creating new opportunities to transform how supply chains are designed, managed, and improved.

We are seeking an Associate Professor/Professor in Supply Chain Management to join the Production Management Research Group at the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) at NTNU, an internationally recognized environment for research in production, logistics, and industrial systems. Supported by the state-of-the-art Logistics 4.0 Lab, the group conducts cutting-edge research in close collaboration with industry and leading international partners, with projects funded by the EU, the Research Council of Norway, and other major funding bodies. We are looking for an experienced researcher who can strengthen and expand our capabilities through research excellence, industry engagement, and external collaboration. You bring a strong understanding of industrial challenges and opportunities, enabling you to build meaningful partnerships and translate research into impact. Through your experience, professional network, and fresh perspectives, you will help shape new research directions, strengthen our collaboration with industry, and further develop our international standing. As part of our group, you will contribute to developing future engineers and managers capable of designing, implementing, and improving integrated supply chains that connect people, products, materials, information, technologies, and resources across the entire value chain.

Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) at NTNU offers a vibrant and interdisciplinary research environment spanning logistics, production management, robotics, product development, materials science, and risk and reliability. We combine academic excellence with strong industrial relevance and are committed to fostering an open, collaborative, and inclusive community. The department offers education at all levels, from Bachelor's and Master's programs to PhD studies, within mechanical- management-, and industrial engineering, along with ICT. 

We welcome candidates who take a holistic and interdisciplinary approach to supply chain management, combining perspectives from industrial engineering and management, and decision science, with computer science, social science, natural science. Particular interest will be given to research addressing the role of emerging technologies, such as AI and digital technologies in enabling resilient, sustainable, circular, and high-performing supply chains that support the future of Norwegian and global industry, as well as their seamless integration in raw material sourcing, product development and supply chain design, and end-of-life product and material recovery and r-strategies.

Your immediate leader is Head of Department.
Duties of the position
• international level research in the scientific area of ​​supply chain management, resulting in publications in internationally top ranked journals in your field
• actively build and maintain industrial supply chain network in Norway  
• initiate new research projects through active interaction with industry and the funding bodies (e.g. EU and The Norwegian Research Council)
• initiate, participate in, and manage externally and internally funded research projects
• contributing to, fronting and leading the development of the research area within your field of research
• teaching at bachelor, master and PhD levels in all the study programs taught in the department
• supervision of bachelor, master and PhD students and provide mentorship to Postdocs and researchers
• contribute to the development and the activities of the Logistics4.0 Lab
• exam preparation and evaluation
• administrative tasks as requiredRequired qualifications 
You must have the qualifications required for the position of Professor or Associate Professor in the field of supply chain management, as outlined in the regulations concerning appointment and promotion to teaching and research posts.

To qualify for this Professor or Associate Professor position, we require the following:

• your academic research production must be within the field of supply chain management  
• you must have minimum 5 year of experience (after PhD) either from supply chain work in industry or research in academia
• you must document a track record of collecting external research  funding if your work experience is from academia
• you must have experience of applying qualitative methodologies, in particular case research, action research, conceptual modelling in supply chain management.
• you must have experience of applying quantitative methodologies, in particular analytical modelling and data-driven (AI-based) modelling, and knowledge in programming and simulation tools for supply chain management.
• you must have publications in highly ranked journals in your field. Scientific articles published in the last five years (excluding career breaks) with relevance for the research areas mentioned above and where interdisciplinary approaches are used will weigh strongest in the evaluation and ranking. The scientific publication record will be evaluated in light of the length of the applicant's academic career taking into account the research field.
• you must have documented experience as researcher/post-doc or equivalent.
• you must have documented experience at least in preparing research funding applications (EU level will be preferred) and you must show ability to define proper attractive research. About Us
At No Isolation, we’re a profitable, 65-person Norwegian EdTech scale-up operating across Europe. We help educators bring learning and belonging to every child.

Our AV1 robot is deployed in 19 countries, with 5,000+ units supporting schools to improve attendance, belonging, and continuity of learning for children who cannot be physically present. Consistently described as life-changing, it bridges the gap between the student and their peers, restoring both educational continuity and the essential sense of social belonging.

We’re established enough to have a proven solution and strong financial foundations, yet still small enough for every new colleague to have a visible impact on our next stage of growth.

The Opportunity - Head of Sales, Nordics
You’ve led sales teams selling to kommuner and other public sector clients. You know how to multi-thread across multiple stakeholders, navigate decision and budget processes, and like being hands-on the most important of deals. Now you want a new challenge with a strong team to develop, and a solution customers actually need and want.

The Nordics are our home market - with some of our best market penetration, where customers rarely churn, yet with lots of market opportunity still to capture. We’re looking for someone who will lead from the front and help a small team across Norway, Sweden and Denmark drive our growth.

What your week looks like
• 
Joining your Account Managers in their customer meetings and helping them close.

• 
Deal reviews and pipeline check-ins with the team.

• 
Working with Marketing, Product and Customer Success on what’s coming next.

• 
Attending and speaking at industry events where our customers are.

What you’ll own
• 
Your own portfolio of key municipal and education accounts, from first meeting to signed agreement.

• 
The move from single-school sales to framework agreements with kommuner and education authorities.

• 
The team’s results across three markets that each need their own plan.

• 
Where we focus: which segments, territories and accounts are worth the push.

• 
A pipeline and forecast in HubSpot that you’re happy to stand behind.

You are probably someone who
• 
Has a track record leading B2B/B2G sales teams - ideally has sold to Norwegian kommuner or other public sector clients, and knows how budgets, politics and procurement work. Experience from other Nordic countries or the Baltics is a plus.

• 
Until recently carried a quota, and/or has remained heavily involved in shaping and closing deals yourself.

• 
Has led and coached account managers, and knows that different people need different support to improve and perform their best.

• 
Understands the importance of sales methodologies, whether that’s MEDDPICC, SPIN, Challenger or similar.

• 
Is data driven and uses CRM (HubSPot a plus) to understand trends and drive performance.

• 
Speaks fluent Norwegian and English. Swedish or Danish is a bonus.

• 
Is based in Oslo and happy with a hybrid setup.

Who you’ll work with
You’ll report to our CCO, Sanjeev, who is based in London and previously led Vodafone business units across Africa and Europe. From our Oslo HQ you’ll work closely with our CEO, Morten, a former McKinsey Partner, and an experienced Leadership Team.

What’s in it for you
• 
Real earning potential. We offer uncapped commission beyond OTE. The need is high and the solution proven - it now requires someone to drive systematic execution.

• 
A solution that sells. It’s unique, backed by evidence of impact and significantly more cost-effective compared to alternatives. Our churn is very low - the solution works and customers love it.

• 
Something to build on. You’re taking over a successful team that now needs taking up to the next level.

• 
A place people like working. Our engagement scores are above benchmark, and we have structured onboarding with a buddy, an annual company trip and great collaboration across teams.

• 
Enhanced parental and sick leave.

• 
Flexible hours around a 10:00–15:00 core, with the option to work remotely.

• 
Central office in Oslo.

• 
27 vacation days.

• 
Travel insurance for you and your immediate family.

• 
Mobile phone and internet subscription.

Location
This role is based in our Oslo HQ office, with regular travel across Norway, Sweden and Denmark to support your team in the field.

We believe in-person leadership matters, so we work a flexible hybrid model built around real collaboration.

How to Apply
Please click Apply and upload your CV in English.

If you’d like, you can also include a short video (in English) as part of your application – this is optional, but it gives us a chance to see a bit more of who you are beyond your CV. Let your personality and passion shine!

If you're looking for a leadership role where the demand is already proven and the job is to build on that - not create it from scratch - we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
The position
Faculty of Humanities and education, The Department of Science and Mathematics at Volda University College invites applications for a three-year PhD Position in mathematics education, artificial intelligence (AI) and competence development.

The position is linked to research activities within TRUST (The Norwegian Centre for Trustworthy AI), one of Norway’s national research centres for artificial intelligence. 

The successful candidate will apply for admission to the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture at Volda University College. The programme takes an interdisciplinary approach, incorporating perspectives on teaching and learning across different subject areas.

The PhD project will be developed in close collaboration with the supervisors within the research framework outlined in this announcement. The candidate is expected to start as soon as possible after appointment.
The research project
Artificial intelligence is transforming education, working life and society, creating a need for new knowledge about the competencies people require in an AI-rich society. The project focuses particularly on mathematical competencies relevant to the development, use and understanding of AI, including modelling, abstraction, statistical reasoning and algorithmic thinking.

The candidate will develop an independent doctoral research project within this broad framework. Possible areas of investigation may include:

• which mathematical and AI-related competencies will become important in a society shaped by AI
• how such competencies are integrated into education and can be developed through educational practice
• how teaching approaches, learning resources and initiatives for competence development can be designed
• how such initiatives can be investigated and evaluated in authentic educational settings
• how AI may shape students’ opportunities for mathematics learning, academic support and developing life skills across home, school and everyday settings
• how these changes may help reduce social and educational inequalities and support participation and democratic development
The project will be rooted in mathematics education research. The final research questions, theoretical framework and research design will be developed in collaboration with the supervisors.

Through TRUST – The Norwegian Centre for Trustworthy AI, and its more than 70 national and international partners from academia, industry, government, and civil society, the candidate will have access to an extensive national and international research network.

TRUST is advancing trustworthy AI that is accurate, interpretable, inclusive, fair, safe, sustainable and well governed. Combining expertise in (i) machine learning, statistics, mathematics, and data science, (ii) law, and social sciences, and (iii) philosophy, the centre develops AI technologies and interdisciplinary frameworks, supports innovation and examines AI’s impact on democracy, the rule of law, and the environment. Research spans theoretical, methodological, legal and empirical perspectives, tested in real-world contexts, including healthcare, mobility, governance, security, and climate resilience. Users, citizens and civil society organisations contribute to assessing the trustworthiness of research and innovation. 

TRUST is funded by the Research Council of Norway and public and private partners, and is led by the University of Oslo, SINTEF and the Norwegian Computing Center (NR). 
Responsibilities
The candidate will:

• carry out an independent doctoral research project
• plan and conduct research activities and data collection
• analyse research data and publish findings
• disseminate research through academic publications, conferences and other relevant forums
• participate actively in the research community at Volda University College and in TRUST-related activities
• collaborate with national and international research partners and practitionersRequired qualifications
Applicants must have:

• a master’s degree or equivalent qualification in mathematics education, mathematics, computing education, educational sciences or a closely related field
• an academic background qualifying for admission to the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture at Volda University College, normally with grades equivalent to B or higher
• good spoken and written English skills
Desirable qualifications

We particularly welcome applicants who can demonstrate one or more of the following:

• documented competence in mathematics teaching or mathematics education, for example through teaching, research, development work or teacher education

jobs.occupation: Stipendiat i flerspråklighet og tverrspråklig påvirkning
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig stilling som stipendiat i flerspråklighet og tverrspråklig påvirkning ved Fakultet for utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora, Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap. Stillingen er ledig fra 01.03.2027

Stipendiatstillingen leder fram til doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen opparbeider du kunnskap, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innenfor forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.

Den som ansettes tas opp på doktorgradsprogrammet i utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora. Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø, samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.
 
Stillingen er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning, eller fire år med forskerutdanning kombinert med annet karrierefremmende arbeid. Dette avklares i rekrutteringsprosessen.

Som stipendiat ved UiS får du støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling gjennom veiledning, kompetanseutvikling og karriereplanlegging.
Forskningstema
Den som ansettes vil være tilknyttet forskergruppen FLUENT (Flerspråklig Utvikling og Endring i Nyere Tid) og Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap. FLUENT forsker på flerspråklighet fra ulike perspektiver, inkludert tilegnelses-, formelle og utdanningsvitenskapelige perspektiver. Forskergruppen er tverrfaglig og åpen for ulike teoretiske og metodiske tilnærminger.

Denne stipendiatstillingen er en åpen utlysning for doktorgradsprosjekter innen flerspråklighet, med særlig fokus på tverrspråklig påvirkning (cross-linguistic influence, CLI) hos to- og flerspråklige talere. Målet er å bidra til økt forståelse av hvordan språk påvirker hverandre i flerspråklige språksystemer, og i hvilken grad grammatiske systemer deles mellom språk.

Selv om tverrspråklig påvirkning er et veletablert fenomen, er det fortsatt mye vi ikke vet om hvilke faktorer som påvirker denne prosessen. Særlig er det behov for mer kunnskap om hvordan språkenes egenskaper og den språklige avstanden mellom dem har en effekt på tverrspråklig påvirkning. Videre er det behov for mer forskning på hvordan ulike typer flerspråklige talere (for eksempel barn og voksne, tidlige og sene tospråklige) og individuelle faktorer som språkferdighet, eksponering og språkbruk påvirker slike prosesser. Fordi mye av tidligere forskning har basert seg på offline- metoder, som for eksempel grammatikalitetsvurderinger, vet vi relativt lite om hvordan tverrspråklig påvirkning kommer til uttrykk mens flerspråklige talere prosesserer språk i sanntid.

Doktorgradsprosjektet skal bidra med ny empirisk kunnskap om tverrspråklig påvirkning ved hjelp av offline-, online- eller kombinerte metodiske tilnærminger. Søkere oppfordres til å utvikle sitt eget prosjekt innenfor dette brede forskningstemaet.

Mulige tema for doktorgradsprosjektet inkluderer, men er ikke begrenset til:

• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning varierer som følge av språklig avstand mellom språk
• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning varierer mellom ulike språklige nivåer, som syntaks, morfologi, ordforråd og fonologi
• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning varierer mellom ulike typer flerspråklige, for eksempel barn og voksne, tidlige og sene tospråklige eller tredjespråksinnlærere
• i hvilken grad individuelle faktorer, som språkferdighet, språklig eksponering og språkbruk, påvirker tverrspråklig påvirkning
• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning kommer til uttrykk på samme eller ulike måter i flerspråkliges språklige kunnskap og i språkprosessering i sanntid 
Prosjekter kan omhandle et bredt spekter av språkkombinasjoner. Prosjekter som inkluderer norsk i kombinasjon med ett eller flere andre språk er særlig relevante, men også andre språkkombinasjoner er velkomne. Stavangers flerspråklige befolkning gir gode muligheter for rekruttering av deltakere med ulike språkbakgrunner.

Avhandlingen skal skrives på engelsk.
Prosjektskisse
Som søker skal du utarbeide en foreløpig prosjektskisse for et doktorgradsprosjekt innenfor det beskrevne forskningstemaet.

Prosjektskissen skal redegjøre for prosjektets problemstilling, relevans, samt teoretisk og metodisk tilnærming. Prosjektskissen, som bør være på ca. 4-5 sider, vil inngå i kompetansevurderingen. 

Dersom du blir ansatt, vil prosjektskissen og prosjektets framdriftsplan videreutvikles i samarbeid med veilederne i løpet av de tre første månedene av ansettelsesperioden og danne grunnlag for den endelige planen for doktorgradsprosjektet. Mal for prosjektskisse finner du her. Prosjektskissen skal skrives på engelsk.
Kvalifikasjoner
Du må ha en sterk faglig bakgrunn med femårig mastergrad innenfor språkvitenskap (linguistics), flerspråklighet, psykolingvistikk, anvendt språkvitenskap, nordisk språk, engelsk språk eller tilsvarende utdanning som gir grunnlag for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning, fortrinnsvis av nyere dato.

Karakter på masteroppgaven og veid gjennomsnittskarakter for masterstudiet må begge tilsvare B eller bedre. 

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.
 
Vi legger også vekt på at du:

• har interesse for forskning på flerspråklighet, språktilegnelse og/eller språkprosessering 
• har erfaring med språkvitenskapelig forskning og gjerne eksperimentelle eller kvantitative metoder
• har høy faglig integritet og fokus på kvalitet i arbeidet
• er nysgjerrig og motivert for å gjennomføre forskningsprosjektet og bidra til faglige fellesskap og samarbeid på tvers av fagområder
• har potensial for forskning innenfor fagfeltet og personlige forutsetninger for å fullføre doktorgradsutdanningen innen ansettelsesperioden
• kan arbeide godt både selvstendig og i samarbeid med andre forskere
• har evne til kritisk refleksjon, nytenkning og selvstendig problemløsning, og arbeider strukturert og målrettet
• har gode samarbeids- og kommunikasjonsevner og bidrar til et konstruktivt arbeidsmiljø.
• har gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig.Krav til engelskkunnskaper
Gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig, er en forutsetning for opptak til doktorgradsprogrammet. 

Dersom du er internasjonal søker og ikke omfattes av fritaksordningene nedenfor, må du dokumentere engelskkunnskapene dine med et gyldig resultat fra én av følgende språktester:

• TOEFL – Test of English as a Foreign Language, Internet-Based Test (IBT). Minimum resultat: 90/4.5
• IELTS – International English Language Testing Service. Minimum resultat: 6.5
• Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) eller Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) fra Universitetet i Cambridge
• PTE Academic – Pearson Test of English Academic. Minimum resultat: 62
Du er fritatt fra kravet dersom du:

• har fullført minst ett års universitetsstudier i Australia, Canada, Irland, New Zealand, Storbritannia eller USA
• har fullført en mastergrad med engelsk som undervisningsspråk i et EU-/EØS-land eller i India
• er fritatt i henhold til HK-dirs GSU liste
• ikke inngår i de ovennevnte unntakskategoriene, men har bodd i Norge de siste fem åreneSom stipendiat ved UiS får du
• forskerutdanning ved et universitet med et viktig samfunnsoppdrag
• et ambisiøst og inkluderende forskningsmiljø
• veiledning og støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling
• gratis norskkurs dersom du ikke behersker norsk, svensk eller dansk på minimum A2-nivå ved ansettelse
• tilgang til Lifekeys, en digital tjeneste for mental helse og livskvalitet
• lønn som stipendiat etter Statens lønnsregulativ i stillingskode 1017, kr 580.000 brutto pr år, med lønnsutvikling etter ansiennitet i stillingen. 
• medlemskap i Statens pensjonskasse med gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger
Les mer om ansattgoder og fordeler på uis.no.
Mangfold og inkludering
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  
Har du spørsmål?
Ta gjerne kontakt dersom du ønsker å vite mer om stillingen og prosjektbeskrivelse:

• Førsteamanuensis Brechje van Osch, e-post: brechje.a.osch@uis.no 
• Førsteamanuensis Yvonne van Baal, e-post: yvonne.w.vanbaal@uis.no .
Har du spørsmål om ansettelsesprosessen, kan du kontakte: 

• HR- rådgiver Christine Valvik., tlf: 51 83 24 23, e-post: christine.valvik@uis.noSlik søker du
Søk stillingen ved å klikke på "Søk stillingen" på denne siden. 

I Jobbnorge registrerer du søknad, relevant utdanning og arbeidserfaring samt språkferdigheter. I søknaden ber vi deg beskrive dine forskningsinteresser, din motivasjon for stillingen og hvordan din bakgrunn er relevant for forskningsprosjektet.

Følgende dokumentasjon skal lastes opp som vedlegg til søknaden:

• prosjektskisse, se mal tilgjengelig på våre nettsider
• CV med fullstendig oversikt over utdanning, erfaring og eventuell vitenskapelig virksomhet
• vitnemål med karakterutskrift som dokumenterer fullført mastergrad. Dersom du ikke har fullført mastergraden, skal du legge ved oppdatert karakterutskrift.
• Diploma Supplement eller tilsvarende dokumentasjon, samt konverteringsskala dersom dette er påkrevd
• dokumentasjon på engelskspråklig kompetanse dersom dette er påkrevd
• publikasjoner eller annet relevant forskningsarbeid
• attester og annen dokumentasjon som vurderes relevant for søknaden 
Dokumentasjonen må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. 

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. Sørg derfor for at søknaden tydelig viser hvordan din kompetanse og erfaring oppfyller kompetansekravene i utlysningen, og at nødvendig dokumentasjon er lastet opp. Dersom vedleggene samlet overskrider 100 MB, må filene komprimeres før opplasting.

UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Opplysninger om søkere kan bli offentliggjort selv om det er bedt om unntak fra offentlig søkerliste, jf. offentlighetsloven § 25. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge, vil du bli varslet.
Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. På bakgrunn av komiteens vurdering vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Les mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den norske teksten som legges til grunn.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Universitetet i Stavanger (UiS) har omlag 12.000 studenter og 1.900 ansatte. Universitetet har store ambisjoner. Vi skal ha en innovativ og internasjonal profil og være en drivkraft i kunnskapsutviklingen og endringsprosesser i samfunnet. Vår felles retning skal drives frem av omtanke for bærekraftig omstilling og rettferdig samfunnsutvikling, gjennom nye måter å forvalte naturressursene på og legge til rette for bedre byer og lokalsamfunn. Energi, helse og velferd, læring for livet er våre satsingsområder.I samspill og dialog med våre omgivelser regionalt, nasjonalt og internasjonalt har vi et åpent og innovativt klima for utdanning, forskning, kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid, nyskapning, formidling og museumsvirksomhet. Den faglige virksomheten ved universitetet er organisert i seks fakultet med 13 institutt og to nasjonale forsknings- og kompetansesenter i tillegg til Arkeologisk museum. Vi er medlem i det europeiske nettverket for innovative universitet - European Consortium of Innovative Universities. Universitetet ligger i den mest attraktive regionen i landet med 300.000 innbyggere.  Stavangerregionen har et dynamisk arbeidsmarked og tilbyr en rekke spennende kultur- og fritidsaktiviteter.Sammen med våre ansatte og studenter vil vi løfte blikket, og våge å tenke stort og nytt – vi vil utfordre det velkjente og utforske det ukjentee.

 

Fakultet for utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora er regionens viktigste institusjon for utdanning av lærere til barnehage, grunnskole, videregående skole, høyskole og universitet. Fakultetet tilbyr også grunnutdanning innenfor idrett, språk, religion, historie, samt åtte masterprogrammer og en doktorgradsutdanning. Fakultetet har tre nasjonale sentre: Nasjonalt lesesenter, Nasjonalt senter for læringsmiljø og atferdsforskning (Læringsmiljøsenteret) og Kunnskapssenter for utdanning (KSU), samt forskningssentrene Filiorum - Senter for barnehageforskning og Greenhouse – Centre for environmental humanities. I tillegg er fakultetet en av fem universitetspartnere i Senter for spesialpedagogisk forskning og inkludering (SpedAims). Fakultetet samarbeider med Utdanningsdirektoratet, kommuner og fylkeskommuner om etter- og videreutdanning av ansatte i barnehage, skole og PPT. Fakultetet har ca. 3.300 studenter, og ca. 400 ansatte fordelt på fakultetsadministrasjonen, Institutt for barnehagelærerutdanning, Institutt for grunnskolelærerutdanning, idrett og spesialpedagogikk, Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap, Nasjonalt lesesenter, Læringsmiljøsenteret og Kunnskapssenter for utdanning.Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap har ansvar for universitetets lektorutdanning for trinn 8-13 og praktisk-pedagogisk utdanning. Instituttet tilbyr også utdanninger innenfor nordisk, engelsk, religion, historie, norsk for internasjonale studenter, og mastergradsutdanninger i historie og historiekultur, nordisk og lesevitenskap, samt engelsk og Literacy Studies. I tillegg har instituttet ansvar for det tverrfakultære årsstudiet Filosofi, politikk og økonomi (PPE), det engelskspråklige masterprogrammet Public Environmental Humanities og et deltidsstudium i museumspedagogikk. I samarbeid med andre enheter ved fakultetet tilbys doktorgradsutdanning i utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora. Det er i dag ca. 70 ansatte og ca. 800 studenter tilknyttet instituttet.

There are two research assistant vacancies linked to VaccAI and CuratedAI at the Department of Information Science and Media Studies, University of Bergen, in the MediaFutures research environment. The positions will support research led by Professor Christoph Trattner.

• VaccAI: one 40% position starting as soon as possible after the application deadline of 15 November 2026, by agreement, and ending on 30 September 2028.
• CuratedAI: one 30% position starting as soon as possible after the application deadline of 15 November 2026, by agreement, and ending on 30 September 2028.
Research assistant is a recruitment position supporting academic staff in their teaching and research. The positions provide an opportunity to gain insight into scientific work and methodology. Total employment as a research assistant cannot exceed two years.
About the projects
VaccAI is a Research Council of Norway funded project examining vaccine related claims in the news and the information environment surrounding vaccination. The project combines analysis of news content with research on how people encounter and evaluate health information. Research assistants will help prepare and analyse research material and support empirical studies of vaccine communication and AI assisted approaches to assessing claims.

CuratedAI is a Research Council of Norway funded project examining artificial intelligence and transparency in journalism. It investigates how the use of AI in producing and verifying news can be communicated to audiences, and how transparency measures affect their understanding and evaluation of news. The research includes AI disclosure, provenance and watermarking approaches, and the needs of journalists and the public.

About MediaFutures

MediaFutures is a Centre for Research based Innovation hosted by the Department of Information Science and Media Studies at the University of Bergen, with its primary workplace at Media City Bergen. In collaboration with news media and technology partners, the centre develops responsible media technology and investigates media experiences, recommender systems, content production and analysis, and audience interaction. Read more at www.mediafutures.no.

The research assistants will formally report to the PI of the two projects Professor Christoph Trattner and support the relevant project teams in scientific, technical and project related administrative tasks. Tasks may include:

• Preparing, collecting, cleaning and documenting research data, including news content, survey responses and experimental data.
• Programming research tools, setting up study infrastructure and supporting online surveys and experiments.
• Reviewing literature, annotating research material and assisting with quantitative or qualitative analyses.
• Contributing to research documentation, reports, publications and dissemination activities.
• Providing practical and administrative support directly related to the assigned project.

• Experience with data collection, data analysis, surveys or experiments is an advantage.
• An interest in health communication and vaccine information is relevant to VaccAI; an interest in journalism, AI transparency and audience research is relevant to CuratedAI.
• Knowledge of the MediaFutures research environment and the media or technology sector is an advantage.We can offer
• A good and professionally challenging working environment, with opportunities to gain practical research experience.

For candidates with a bachelor’s degree (code 1019), the gross annual salary will be NOK 470 200.-. For candidates with a master’s degree (code 1020), the annual salary will be NOK 519 400,-. The salary mentioned is for a 100% position. 
• Enrolment in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund and good welfare benefits.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

A PhD position in Societal readiness for AI-supported life cycle assessment in the architecture, engineering, and construction sectors is now open at the Energy and Environment Group at the Department of Architecture and Technology, NTNU. The Energy and Environment Group lead centres/projects like the Research centre on zero emission neighbourhoods in smart cities (ZEN), syn.ikia – Sustainable plus energy neighbourhoods, and the Green Deal ARV project on Climate positive circular communities. We use real demonstration projects and our laboratory facilities (like the ZEB laboratory) extensively in our research. The group currently comprises 10 senior staff members (professors and associate professors), and around 20 research fellows (research assistants, PhD candidates, and post-doctoral researchers). The duration of the position is 3 years.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
Life Cycle Assessment is a key instrument for environmental governance in the architecture, engineering, and construction industry. At the same time, new artificial intelligence (AI) based tools are beginning to automate central parts of the LCA-based design practice. This includes data gathering, model construction, scenario generation, results interpretation, and decision support. This development may increase speed and usability, especially in early-stage design, but it also raises important questions about transparency, methodological integrity, accountability, professional judgement, and institutional preparedness. 

This PhD project will examine the societal readiness of the architecture, engineering, and construction sectors for AI-supported environmental assessments. The use of AI-supported LCA tools will be studied through case applications, including usage of machine-learning approaches, large language models, and automated workflows. The project will analyze how such tools reshape trust, responsibility, accountability, and professional judgement in environmental decision-making, by adopting a mixed-method approach.

The project will be carried out at the Department of Architecture and Technology at NTNU, in cooperation with SINTEF Industry, department of Manufacturing and NTNU Social Research.

The immediate leader is head of department. The place of duty is Trondheim.

• Carry out research of high quality on AI-assisted LCA in-light of applied use, environmental governance challenges, and societal readiness.

jobs.occupation: Kongsberg Maritime seeks Naval Architect/Ship Designer
jobs.description:
Do you have a passion for ship design and want to work on some of the world’s most advanced specialized vessels? Kongsberg Maritime is a technology pioneer, enabling a more sustainable future for our oceans. Our zero-emission integrated technologies advance the maritime industry and solve our customers' toughest problems. We are currently in an exciting growth phase and are seeking an experienced Naval Architect to join our award-winning Ship Design Solutions team.As a designer with us, you become part of an environment with over 50 years of history and a portfolio of over 1,000 vessels. We are leading the green shift at sea, and you will play a central role in the evolution of our renowned UT and NVC designs, with a particular focus on decarbonization and innovative technological solutions.
Key Responsibilities

As a Ship Designer, you will hold an autonomous and customer-oriented role. Your main tasks will include:

• Design Leadership: Acting as the design responsible for dedicated customer projects and R&D programs, managing supporting teams as required.
• Technical Development: Taking primary responsibility for General Arrangements, vessel specifications, and performance documentation from initial customer meetings through to contract.
• Strategic Collaboration: Engaging in dialogue with ship owners, yards, and classification societies to understand market trends and regulatory requirements.
• Sales & Marketing Support: Contributing to bid/no-bid evaluations and supporting the sales force with technical expertise and tender documentation.
• Innovation: Being a driving force in the technological evolution of our portfolio, specifically within offshore, navy, and unmanned vessels.Your Profile

We are looking for a candidate who possesses a holistic understanding of ship structures and the ability to think across a diverse design portfolio.

• Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Naval Architecture or a related engineering field.
• Ideally 5 years of relevant experience from a shipyard, classification society, or consultancy. 
• Proficiency in AutoCAD is required. Interest in 3D tools (Revit), visualization (Rhino), or CFD (Star-CCM+) is a plus.
• Fluent in English, as this is our primary working language for projects and international collaboration.
This employment may require a pre-employment check procedure in accordance with company security standards, role or site requirements. Please note that this might affect the offer process or employment
Why Join Kongsberg Maritime?
• Innovation in Focus: Work with tomorrow’s solutions in unmanned vessels and green shipping.
• Career Development: We offer excellent programs for competence building and internal career paths.
• Social Environment: Enjoy an active corporate sports club and social groups ranging from mountain hiking and fishing to wine tasting.
